findings.finding: BETA has beaten the TOP of its own quarterly revenue guide on both 2026 prints (Q1 $10.13m vs $7-10m guide; Q2 $14.66m vs $8-11m, 33% over the top end, driven by EPFD and Florida DOT charger deliveries); Q3 is guided $8-12m with consensus $10.77m, so a repeat of the pattern implies ~$12-14m, i.e. ~+10-30% vs consensus - but this stock fell -2.58% and -3.29% on the last two beats, the second with a FY revenue raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 revenue beat top of guide: -2.58% (2026-05-12). Q2 2026 beat top of guide by 33% and raised FY revenue guide to $42-50m: -3.29% (2026-08-12). Beats have been sold on both occasions.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 (Aviation Week, NBAA) CEO Kyle Clark said CX300 certification is 'taking longer than he initially expected' and listed 'motor certification' among goals for 'the year ahead' - the H500A engine, guided to FAA type certification in H1 2026 and described in July as 'closing in', is still uncertified - while 2027 revenue consensus is $361.65m (vs ~$47m for 2026), a ramp that requires CX300 certification and deliveries; the Q3 release/call is the first formal venue to restate (likely push out) certification timing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The H1 2026 H500A target slipped at the Q1 print (2026-05-12, -2.58%, together with an EBITDA guide cut); price targets were cut by Citi ($33->$25), BTIG ($40->$33) and Cantor ($38->$31) around that time citing revised delivery expectations. No print yet has carried a dated CX300 slip.

findings.finding: The EXIM financing expansion of up to $1bn net ($830m incremental, non-dilutive) announced 2026-08-04 was only an 'intent', subject to due diligence and definitive documentation, and no press release or 8-K since (EDGAR shows no 8-K after August) reports it closing; a closing or a firm timeline announced with Q3 would remove the dilution overhang on a company burning ~$400-445m adj. EBITDA plus $150-200m capex a year against $1.48bn cash.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Announcement of intent on 2026-08-04 was not a print; no print-day history on financing.

findings.finding: FAA granted BETA a Special Airworthiness Certificate for market surveys on the ALIA A250 eVTOL (announced 2026-10-21, first such authorization for an eVTOL; first flight Plattsburgh-Burlington 20 Oct), and BETA completed 14 all-electric flights in Florida under eIPP (release 2026-10-30) - milestones the Q3 release will restate as the quarter's highlights.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Stock rose 6.1% on 2026-10-21 on the authorization (MarketBeat item per search); not a print-day item.

findings.finding: CEO Kyle Clark's Godric's Hollow Trust has sold 10,000 shares a day under a 10b5-1 plan through the run-in (Form 4s filed twice weekly 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-30, e.g. 30,000 shares on 28-30 Oct at $19.92-20.61; 4.97m shares remain in the trust) - about 1% of daily volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print-day history; similar plan sales ran through the Aug print.

findings.finding: Short interest nearly doubled into the print, from 7.8m shares (3.3% of float, 2026-08-20) to 14.59m shares at 8.0 days to cover (2026-10-15), roughly 12% of a ~117.6m Class A float, while put/call open interest is 0.4 - a growing short base that a better-than-feared certification update or EXIM closing would have to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with this short base; short interest was ~3-5% of float at the August print (-3.29%).

findings.finding: Sell-side lowered the loss bar into the print: Q3 EPS consensus moved from -$0.51 to -$0.62 over the last 30 days with one downward revision for Q3, Q4, FY26 and FY27 and none upward, while the company's own Q3 adj. EBITDA guide (-$115m to -$125m) is unchanged since August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 adj. EBITDA landed at the midpoint of its -$100m to -$120m guide (-$109.8m); stock -3.29%. The EBITDA guide was widened at Q1 (-2.58%).

outside_window.finding: Joby Aviation reports Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-11-04, after BETA's exit window closes; an eVTOL-sector read-across (certification, cash burn) can move BETA only after the trade has ended.

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; beats sold twice): revenue-beat finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, and print_vs_bar trimmed from +16% to +12% because the Q2 overshoot was partly one-off charger deliveries.
Lesson 7 (positioning): certification-slip negative agrees with the +6.6 put skew (likely priced) and sits on ~12% of float short at 8 DTC - cut from -2.0 to -1.5; p_up moved from 46 to 47.
Lesson 5 (inference/thin bar): EPS-revision finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1 because only two analysts carry EPS and the sources disagree.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): EXIM finding kept positive at +0.3 after checking the money funds a ramp corroborated by a $3.9bn backlog.
Lesson 6 (bar and window): bar sourced to company guide plus three agreeing estimate sources; Joby read-across kept in outside_window; nothing else changed.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue run-rate inference: Q3 2025 revenue was $3.08bn and Q2 2025 was $2.96bn, so last year's Q2-to-Q3 step was +3.9%. The same step on Q2 2026's $3,333.9M gives about $3.46bn. Separately, CF grew 8% in H1 2026, and 8% on Q3 2025 CF of about $3.04bn plus about $0.16bn of Casgevy, Journavx and one month of Palsonify gives about $3.45bn. Both are about 1-1.5% above the $3.40-3.42bn consensus. Consensus already implies CF growth slowing to about 7%, which management flagged (smaller prior-year US price and FX contribution in H2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $3.33bn against a $3.22bn consensus (+3.5%) with a guide raise; the stock moved +1.7% close-to-close. Q1 2026 was a revenue miss and the stock moved -1.3%. Q3 2025: a small beat with Casgevy short; -1.0%. Sources: https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/vrtx-implied-move and https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/26/the-500-million-non-cf-factor-vertex-investors-cant-ignore-on-nov-2/

findings.finding: FX swings from a tailwind to a small headwind in Q3. EUR/USD averaged about 1.151 in Q3 2026 (Jul 1.1425, Aug 1.1588, Sep 1.1511) against about 1.169 in Q3 2025 (Jul 1.1680, Aug 1.1640, Sep 1.1735), a weaker euro by about 1.5% YoY. The FY guide assumed about +150bp of FX benefit, earned mostly in H1. Ex-US revenue was $1.28bn of $3.33bn in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No VRTX print traced to FX in the sources found. Management called out FX contributing less in H2 on the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15381606277997568).

findings.finding: Journavx Q2 revenue ($49.6M, +71% sequential) was helped by a wholesaler channel build after a Q1 drawdown. Management warned of 'some quarterly volatility in inventory build and drawdown' and pushed gross-to-net normalisation out to H1 2027, with the patient support programme used more than forecast. So Q3 Journavx revenue can lag script growth (Q2 scripts about 535k, +45% sequential) or step down sequentially if the channel unwinds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: Journavx came in just short of expectations ($19.6M) and Casgevy missed ($16.9M against a $35M model); the stock moved -1.0% close-to-close (https://www.fiercepharma.com/pharma/vertex-confident-journavxs-launch-despite-falling-short-sales, https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/vrtx-implied-move).

findings.finding: Casgevy has had three straight quarters of more than 100 patient initiations (through Q2 2026). H1 2026 infusions already exceeded all of 2025, Q2 revenue was $76.4M (+78% sequential), and the CFO said Casgevy is the larger contributor to the 'very confident' $500M+ non-CF target. That needs about $300M in H2 against about $200M in H1. The initiation backlog supports another sequential step in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Casgevy missed in Q3 2025 ($16.9M) and the stock moved -1.0%. Q2 2026's Casgevy acceleration came with a +1.7% move.

findings.finding: The first FY26 guide to include Crinetics (closed 2026-09-01) will add Palsonify revenue (Crinetics Q2 2026 net product revenue $24.0M, Q1 $10.3M, so about $35-40M for Sep-Dec). It will also add Crinetics' cost base (Q2 R&D $99.9M plus SG&A $57.6M, about $157M a quarter, so roughly $200M for Sep-Dec) and interest on the $4.5bn term loan, against the current $5.65-5.75bn non-GAAP opex guide, which Vertex is already tracking at the high end. The headline opex guide will rise, and a revenue raise will be partly inorganic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Vertex print carried an acquisition guide rebase in the sources found. The Alpine deal in 2024 brought a $4.4bn AIPR&D charge (https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results references the comparison); its reaction was not sourced.

findings.finding: The Q3 EPS bar is mechanically broken. Published Q3 consensus reads -$1.20 (range -$29.51 to +$5.06) on 247wallst against $4.92 non-GAAP on Earnings Whispers, because some analysts model a Crinetics acquired-IPR&D charge and Vertex includes AIPR&D in non-GAAP. Whether Crinetics is booked as an asset acquisition (charge) or a business combination (no charge) is not disclosed; Vertex said accounting details come on the Q3 call. The headline beat or miss will be an accounting artefact.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not sourced for VRTX. The market has looked through a non-cash AIPR&D charge before (Alpine 2024), but no reaction figure was found.

findings.finding: Several 2H26 pipeline readouts promised in the Q2 release have not been reported and may come with the Q3 release or call: VX-828 next-generation CF proof of concept (Phase 1 NCT06154447 primary completion 2026-07-10), VX-670 DM1 GALILEO results ('complete dosing and share results in 2H26'), and updated zimislecel / VX-017 type 1 diabetes timelines ('later this year'). The sign is unknown; this widens the distribution.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 4 2025: a pipeline disappointment (pain) alongside the print gave -20.6% close-to-close against a 6.6% implied move (https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/vrtx-implied-move). Pipeline news on print day has been the tail driver for this name.

findings.finding: Run-up and informal bar: VRTX rose from 501.95 (2026-10-19 close) to 558.88 (2026-10-30 close, +11.3%), above its 2026-09-02 all-time high of 555.98, helped by RAINIER Phase 3 povetacicept data in NEJM and at ASN on 2026-10-24 (PDUFA 2026-11-30). The whisper EPS of $5.10 sits above the $4.92 consensus. The stock goes into the print with a raised informal bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: up about 11% into the print window per Earnings Whispers, then +1.7% on a beat and raise. Beats have been bought modestly, not strongly.

findings.finding: The FY revenue consensus may already sit above the guide top. 247wallst carries FY26 consensus at $13.26bn against the $13.1-13.2bn guide (EW carries $13.06bn). Q4 2025 implied about $3.19bn (FY25 $12.00bn less H1 $5.735bn less Q3 $3.08bn), +3.4% on Q3 2025. The same seasonality on a $3.42bn Q3 gives about $13.28bn. An organic guide raise is likely, but if the $13.26bn figure is right it is already in the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide raises: Q2 2026 raise +1.7%; Feb 2026 print +5.7%. No miss-on-guide print found in the sources.

findings.finding: BofA forecasts Q3 Trikafta at $2.42bn, 5% below consensus. Trikafta fell about 2% YoY in Q2 ($2,497.2M) as patients switched to Alyftrek ($573.6M, +35% sequential), so a Trikafta shortfall is largely offset inside total CF.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not sourced at the product line level.

outside_window.finding: Povetacicept (IgAN) FDA PDUFA date. RAINIER interim data were strong (49.8% proteinuria reduction against placebo) and are already public.
AMPLITUDE (inaxaplin, AMKD) interim analysis expected early 2027.
